Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zutempo 0.0.0.9000

  • Operators on dates and times are a zutempo_type_error that names the function to use, such as temporal_add() or temporal_equals(). Before, base R’s operators ran on the stored numbers and gave wrong values (instant(x) + 0.5) or answers that disagreed with temporal_equals() (z1 == z2). min(), max() and range() return a value of the same type, in the order sort() uses; a plain_month_day() has no order, so they are errors there, as sum() and the others are on every type.

  • The system time zone reads TZ in the forms the C library accepts: a leading : is dropped, and a path under a zone directory names its zone. A zone that is set but cannot be read gives "UTC" with a zutempo_tz_warning, where before it gave "UTC" silently.

  • as.POSIXct() and as.POSIXlt() of a zoned value give an offset of -13:00 or -14:00 the tzone "UTC" rather than an Etc/GMT zone tzdata lacks, and keep the tzone of zones that are equal under TimeZoneEquals, such as Asia/Calcutta and Asia/Kolkata. The help page says that as.POSIXlt() of mixed zones does not round-trip.

  • Documentation: a README from Temporal to R, a table of every Temporal member and its R function on each type’s help page, ?zutempo_options for the options the functions share, and articles on the package website: “Get started”, following one zoned value from construction to base R, and articles on plain dates and times, durations, instants and time zones, strings and formatting, and base R and data frames.

  • Checked against test262’s Temporal tests (39,263 cases from 2,715 files) and against base R’s offsets for every zone. Fixes from that: the constructors read a zoned_date_time() (plain_date(z), plain_time(z), plain_date_time(z), instant(z)); relative_to = "-271821-04-19" works; temporal_since() and temporal_until() on year-months raise a range error when the first of a month is not a valid date; a time zone string whose offset has seconds is an error even when they are zero; and a duration field computed from a large total is the nearest double.

  • On macOS the time zone database is R’s own copy first, then the system’s, as base R reads it, so zutempo and POSIXct agree; TZDIR = "macOS" selects the system’s.

  • Operations on zoned values no longer look for the time zone database on every call: the directory is found once per setting of zutempo.tzdir and TZDIR, and again after zutempo_tz_reset(). Many short calls run several times faster.

  • Conversions with base R’s dates and times: as.Date(), as.POSIXct() and as.POSIXlt() on the zutempo types, temporal_to_difftime() for a plain_time() or duration(), and the other way through the constructors: plain_date(<Date>), instant(<POSIXct>), zoned_date_time(<POSIXct>), plain_date_time(<POSIXlt>), plain_time(<difftime>) and duration(<difftime>). A POSIXct is read at its double’s exact value, rounded half to even to the nanosecond, and written as the nearest double second.

  • Strings are read with every RFC 9557 annotation: any number of key-value annotations after the time zone, [u-ca=iso8601] in any case, and the ! critical flag, which makes an unknown annotation or a second calendar an error. A calendar other than ISO 8601 is a zutempo_range_error on the types with a date and is ignored by instant() and plain_time(), as in Temporal. A zutempo_parse_error carries position, the byte where the string failed. Time zone and calendar arguments take an ISO string that names one (time_zone = "2026-03-07T12:00+01:00").

  • temporal_to_string() and format() take the options of each type’s Temporal toString(): fractional_second_digits, smallest_unit and rounding_mode on the types with a time and on durations, calendar_name on the types with a date, and time_zone_name and offset on a zoned_date_time().

  • zutempo_parse(x, type) reads a character vector as any of the eight types, with NA for the strings it cannot read, and zutempo_parse_errors() lists them with their index, byte position, class and message.

  • Zone-aware arithmetic: temporal_add(), temporal_subtract(), temporal_since(), temporal_until() and temporal_round() on a zoned_date_time(), with date units through the calendar in the value’s zone and time units on the exact time, so a day across a clock change is not 24 hours; temporal_get_time_zone_transition(); and temporal_round(), temporal_total() and duration_compare() with a zoned_date_time() as relative_to, where days follow the zone (PT25H rounded to days relative to 2026-03-07 in New York is P1DT2H).

  • zoned_date_time(): Temporal’s ZonedDateTime as an R vector with a time zone per element, from RFC 9557 strings with the zone in brackets ("2026-03-07T12:00[America/New_York]") or from fields with time_zone, resolving clock gaps and folds with disambiguation and a disagreeing UTC offset with offset. Every calendar and clock field, offset(), offset_nanoseconds(), time_zone_id(), hours_in_day(), temporal_start_of_day(), temporal_with(), temporal_with_plain_time(), temporal_with_time_zone(), temporal_to_instant(), the conversions to the plain types, temporal_equals() through TimeZoneEquals, zoned_date_time_compare() and temporal_to_string(); temporal_to_zoned_date_time_iso() on an instant() and temporal_to_zoned_date_time() on a plain_date() or plain_date_time(); now_time_zone_id(), now_zoned_date_time_iso(), now_plain_date_time_iso(), now_plain_date_iso() and now_plain_time_iso(). Mixed zones combine, subset, sort and sit in data frames; vctrs sees a record of instant and zone.

  • Named IANA time zones resolve from the time zone database base R reads, in base R’s lookup order (option zutempo.tzdir, TZDIR, then the platform’s copies), on fat and slim files alike, with case-insensitive identifiers returned in the database’s case. temporal_to_string() on an instant() takes a named time_zone; zutempo_tz_reset() forgets the parsed zones; zutempo_info() reports the database’s directory, tzdata version and form (fat or slim) and the link table’s version. A named zone without a database is a zutempo_tz_error naming the directories tried.

  • instant(): Temporal’s Instant over its full range, from strings with Z or an offset, instant_from_epoch_milliseconds() and instant_from_epoch_nanoseconds() (numbers or decimal strings), with epoch_milliseconds(), epoch_nanoseconds() as a decimal string, instant_compare(), temporal_equals(), temporal_add(), temporal_subtract(), temporal_since(), temporal_until(), temporal_round() as if positive, and temporal_to_string() with a time_zone of "UTC" or a fixed offset; now_instant().

  • duration(): Temporal’s Duration as an R vector of ten exact fields, from fields or ISO 8601 strings, with years() to nanoseconds(), blank(), sign() and abs(), temporal_with(), temporal_negated(), temporal_abs(), temporal_add(), temporal_subtract(), temporal_round(), temporal_total(), duration_compare() and temporal_to_string(); calendar units take relative_to. == compares fields, and < and sort() order durations free of calendar units.

  • temporal_add(), temporal_subtract(), temporal_since() and temporal_until() on plain_date(), plain_time(), plain_date_time() and plain_year_month(), with overflow, largest_unit, smallest_unit, rounding_increment and rounding_mode.

  • plain_year_month() and plain_month_day(): Temporal’s PlainYearMonth and PlainMonthDay as R vectors, from fields, strings or dates, with their fields, temporal_with(), temporal_equals(), plain_year_month_compare(), temporal_to_string() and temporal_to_plain_date() taking the missing day or year; temporal_to_plain_year_month() and temporal_to_plain_month_day() on a plain_date().

  • plain_date(), plain_time() and plain_date_time(): Temporal’s PlainDate, PlainTime and PlainDateTime as R vectors, built from fields with overflow, from ISO 8601 strings, or from each other, with every field accessor (year(), month_code(), day_of_week(), week_of_year(), hour(), …), temporal_with(), temporal_with_plain_time(), temporal_with_calendar(), temporal_to_plain_date(), temporal_to_plain_time(), temporal_to_plain_date_time(), temporal_equals(), the *_compare() statics, temporal_round() with the nine rounding modes, and temporal_to_string(). The vectors subset, combine, sort, print and sit in data frames; vctrs and pillar methods register when those packages load.

  • zutempo_info() reports the package and zufast versions, whether the 128-bit arithmetic uses the compiler’s __int128, and the pinned commits of the Temporal specification and of test262 with the tzdata release the fixtures come from.

  • The condition classes of the design: zutempo_error, zutempo_range_error, zutempo_parse_error, zutempo_type_error and zutempo_tz_error, each carrying the index of the first failing element.
